hook.text: A self-driving car needs to see the world—and cameras are the cheapest way to give it eyes.

buildup.text: Multiple cameras around the car stitch together a full 360-degree view of the surroundings.

discovery.text: Neural networks process the images in real time, identifying lanes, signs, cars, and pedestrians.

twist.text: Cameras fail in the same conditions human eyes do—glare, darkness, and heavy rain blind them.

climax.text: Tesla bet its entire self-driving strategy on cameras alone, while competitors added other sensors.

punchline.text: Cameras see everything cheaply but struggle when humans do too.

quiz.question: Which company bets entirely on cameras for self-driving, without lidar?
